free_tier.stated: European dedicated bare-metal GPU servers sold by the month, which is the cheapest per-hour shape for a workload that runs continuously. The page lists per-card monthly prices only, with no hourly rate, no spot or on-demand tier and no stated minimum bill; the hourly figures are derived at 730 hours and USD 1 = EUR 0.89246: RTX 3090 24GB from EUR 125 per card per month, USD 140.06, USD 0.192/hr; RTX A6000 48GB from EUR 181, USD 202.81, USD 0.278/hr; RTX 4090 24GB from EUR 329, USD 368.64, USD 0.505/hr; RTX 5090 32GB from EUR 499, USD 559.13, USD 0.766/hr; A100 40GB 8x at EUR 363 per card, USD 0.557/hr; L40S 8x at EUR 411, USD 0.631/hr; A100 SXM 80GB 8x at EUR 624, USD 0.958/hr; H100 SXM 8x NVLink at EUR 1,488 per card, USD 1,667.30, USD 2.284/hr; H200 1x at EUR 2,987, USD 4.585/hr. The page lists no L4. Each server ships with the CPU, RAM, NVMe and 1 Gbit network named on the row; the page states no setup fees.

egress.terms: Storage and network are included in the monthly price on this page; egress terms were not published there and were not established.

chaining: A 48 GB A6000 at USD 0.278 per hour is the cheapest 48 GB card found for continuous use, below Massed Compute at USD 0.55 on demand, and it arrives with a whole server's RAM and 2 TB of NVMe rather than a rented slice.

limits.value: The one-month commitment on a bare-metal invoice is the binding term, so the USD 0.192 per hour only exists for a workload that occupies the card for most of 730 hours.
